gap: No result ChatGPT got works out how long each strip's USB-C port takes to refill a laptop. Using Apple's 53.8 Wh 13-inch MacBook Air battery, the 20 W strips (Anker 351, TESSAN PS07, TESSAN Tower) need at least 2.7 h and the Anker 12-in-1 needs 1.5 h, or 2.7 h once a second port is in use. The 65–67 W hubs need about 0.8 h, and the Anker Nano still needs only 1.8 h with all four USB ports busy.
standout_why: LaptopBee has one phone charge time (an iPhone 15 to 50% in about 26 min on an Anker strip) and shared-budget totals, but no laptop hours. iTechGuides says outright that it does not work out laptop charge time or cost per watt. ChatGPT's own answer only says laptops 'benefit from 65W or higher'. I could not open Tom's Guide, the cited page (the fetch returned only its title), so I can't rule out that it has charge times. That is why this scores 2 and not 3.
decides: For phones it confirms the Anker 351, ChatGPT's pick. For anyone who wants to charge a laptop from the strip it overturns that pick: the 351 and the PS07 cap USB-C at 20 W, half of the 40 W adapter Apple ships with the M5 Air. That makes the TESSAN 65 W GaN hub ($29.99, 0.83 h, $0.46 per USB-C watt) or the Anker Nano 67 W the right choice. The Nano is sold out at anker.com.
